### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **1** package(s): `@objectstack/cloud-connection`, touching **13** documentable anchor(s).

**23** hand-written doc(s) name something this change touched — list omitted above 15 rows. Re-derive on the tree named below: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 7cda377c17626047ea4a76dbfd14a6671f089fd7`.

⛔ **4** release-owned page(s) also affected — read-only, see AGENTS.md Documentation Guardrails.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **1** anchor(s) matched too much of the corpus to be a work list: `PERMISSION_DENIED (literal, 39 pages)`
- **1** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **54** of **206** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **152** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **152**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **55** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **97** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **4** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 7cda377c17626047ea4a76dbfd14a6671f089fd7` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `fbaaddccb41a4f293b9108365ab5648f02976ba0` — the merge of head `e9fe7fe9bc75ea20cc85345c161d85ad79d9f5d0` into base `7cda377c17626047ea4a76dbfd14a6671f089fd7`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin fbaaddccb41a4f293b9108365ab5648f02976ba0 && git checkout fbaaddccb41a4f293b9108365ab5648f02976ba0
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 7cda377c17626047ea4a76dbfd14a6671f089fd7 e9fe7fe9bc75ea20cc85345c161d85ad79d9f5d0 && git checkout -B drift-repro 7cda377c17626047ea4a76dbfd14a6671f089fd7 && git merge --no-ff e9fe7fe9bc75ea20cc85345c161d85ad79d9f5d0

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 7cda377c17626047ea4a76dbfd14a6671f089fd7
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 7cda377c17626047ea4a76dbfd14a6671f089fd7` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

Disclosure (the maintainer's ruling recorded on #9387): findings below are stated as behaviour and code locations, with no reproduction.

### ① Derived judgments

Line numbers are the plugin at the head. The boundary as built: `holdsSetupAccess` (`:410-443`), `refuseWithoutSetupAccess` (`:445`), `servedStatus` (`:466-480`), the `status` handler (`:485-531`), and the three door checks at `:558` (`bind/start`), `:619` (`bind/poll`) and `:720` (`unbind`).

1. **Accept-set of `bind/start`, `bind/poll`, `unbind` narrows — right.** A signed-in, un-held session that does not hold `setup.access` is answered `403 PERMISSION_DENIED` naming the capability. The order at each door is unchanged ahead of the new check and the check sits before every effect: unparseable JSON body `400` (`bind/start`, `bind/poll`) → environment `404` → ADR-0069 held-session `403` → anonymous `401` → **`setup.access` `403`** → `CLOUD_UNCONFIGURED` `503` → body validation → every control-plane fetch → every `ConnectionCredentialStore` read, write or clear. Nothing these doors refused on `main` becomes accepted; a holder's path is byte-identical to `main`'s. Because the refusal precedes the `cloudUrl` test, a caller without the capability is not told whether a control plane is configured.

2. **Every credential shape the doors accept, judged — right.** (a) Anonymous: `resolveSession` is null → `401`, as before. (b) An API key alone (`x-api-key`, or `Authorization: Bearer` with the `osk_` prefix — `api-key.ts:82-97`): no session resolves → `401`, as before; these doors admit no key and never did. (c) A key beside a session: the shared resolver's step 1 admits, holds or refuses the key before its session arm runs (`resolve-authz-context.ts`, "API key takes precedence over session"), so `authz.credential` is not `session` — or no principal resolves — and `holdsSetupAccess` answers false → `403`. A refused or lifecycle-refused key beside a holder's session is therefore refused where `main` served the session: a narrowing beyond the card's words, and the resolver's own rule (a refused key never falls through to the session). Observation, not a defect: a lifecycle-refused key here answers `PERMISSION_DENIED` naming `setup.access` rather than the key's located `403` that the install-local doors re-raise, because the `catch` at `:439-442` returns false for every non-outage throw; fail-closed, and the Console panel sends no key. (d) A held session: the ADR-0069 `403` at `:554/:616/:717` comes first, unchanged. (e) The same-principal guard `authz.credential !== 'session' || authz.userId !== caller.userId → false` fails closed on any mismatch.

3. **The shared permission read is reused, not re-spelled — right.** `holdsSetupAccess` reads `resolveAuthzContext(...).systemPermissions` and nothing else, the shape of `resolveInstallPrincipal` / `requireInstallCapability` (`marketplace-install-local-plugin.ts:3365-3505`) and of `admin-routes.ts:504-535`, with the same inputs (`classifyAdmissionTenancyPosture`, `userAuthGateSourceOf`, `apiKeyLifecyclePolicySourceOf`). The aggregation is the resolver's (`resolveUserAuthzGrants`: `sys_member` → `sys_user_position` → permission sets by catalog name; `grantAppliesInTenant` at `resolve-authz-context.ts:855` admits a global row or one scoped to the session's active organization — the organization-administrator shape the pins control for). No `sys_*` read is spelled in the plugin (its only `sys_` strings are comments and control-plane object names); `check:authz-resolver` sits in the green `Lint & Repo Gates` run. The resolver is handed the session this surface already read (its `getSession` input returns that same `sessionData`; no second read), so identity does not move: `resolveSession` stays the one session read for all seven session doors.

4. **Grants come from where the session came from, and no engine fails closed — right.** Multi-tenant: the environment kernel the session was read from (`readFrom.kernel`) answers `objectql` and `tenancy`; single-environment: the host's `objectql` through `ctx.getService`, the host kernel's `tenancy` through `ctx.getKernel?.()`. With no engine the resolver returns a principal with no grants → false. A `tenancy` or `objectql` that was never registered is the quiet path (the loader throws the branded `serviceNotRegisteredError`, `plugin-loader.ts:241`; `classifyAdmissionTenancyPosture` maps that brand to `undefined`), so a lean composition is not turned into an outage.

5. **The outage path fails closed on the doors — right.** `AuthzStoreUnavailableError` — from the resolver's `tryFind` on a read failure that is not a missing table, or from `classifyAdmissionTenancyPosture` on a `tenancy` that broke — is re-raised by `holdsSetupAccess` (`:440`) and escapes the three handlers. The hono adapter's `declaredEnvelopeForThrow` (`adapter.ts:334`, with `resolveThrownHttpError`, `thrown-http-error.ts:206`) renders a throw that declares its status and code; this error declares `503` / `SERVICE_UNAVAILABLE` (`authz-store-unavailable.ts:90-96,151`). So an unreadable store answers `503`, never a `403` that reads as a denial. Pinned ("an outage, not a 403", both modes, no control-plane call).

6. **`status`: accept-set unchanged, served-set narrowed — right.** It still answers every caller `200` and issues no `401`/`403`. `bound`, `runtimeId`, `provider` go to everyone; `environmentId` and the control plane's `connection` record go only when `servedStatus` finds a session that is not held, resolved through the `session` credential as the same user, and holding `setup.access`. Anonymous, signed-in-without, held, key-beside and outage callers all get the narrowed shape, pinned as an exact key set. `connection` no longer passes through verbatim: the control-plane answer is built inside the fetch's `try` and served outside it (`:503-525`), so a fault of `servedStatus` is not swallowed by the fetch's fall-through. Derived consequence, judged right: `status` now reads the session for every caller (and, multi-tenant, calls `kernel-manager.getOrCreate` for the hostname-resolved environment) where it read none before — the card's done-condition (details to a holder) cannot be met otherwise, and the claim's hold-off is honoured in what it meant: `status` refuses nobody and answers a held session narrowed; the auth-gate census pin was rewritten to this contract. Note, pre-existing and unchanged: the runtime's own status fetch to the control plane (with the runtime's credential, never the caller's) still precedes the permission read; the check decides what is served, not whether the runtime asks.

7. **Error code — right.** `PERMISSION_DENIED` is `HttpStatusErrorCodeMap[403]` (`errors.zod.ts:186`); the ledger sends a generic permission condition to the standard catalog rather than a registered synonym (`error-code-ledger.zod.ts`, "Registering a new code"), and `FORBIDDEN` is the #8211-waived synonym that shadows it (`:1761`). Nothing is registered, `packages/spec` is untouched, and the message names the capability and no secret. The conformance suite pins the envelope on all three doors.

8. **Public type face — right, named.** The package-local, non-exported `PluginContext` gained an optional `getKernel?()`, so the exported `CloudConnectionPlugin.start(ctx)` accepts a superset of host contexts; every host that satisfied the old shape satisfies the new one, and core's real `PluginContext.getKernel(): ObjectKernel` (`types.ts:92`, `kernel.ts:861`) is structurally assignable to the optional slot. No wire key, export, option or config field moves. This is not a Clause-② widening (that clause is a new key on a published payload, in the gate's own words) and does not change the `no (narrowing)` declaration. The consumer type-check lane is pending (③).

9. **Pins — right.** 26 new cases, both resolution modes, through the routes `start()` + `kernel:ready` really mount. Grants are real permission-set rows read through `find`, with a `find` double that honours `where` and `limit`, so a grant row cannot be read as everyone's. Each refusal asserts status, code, the declared envelope, zero control-plane calls and an untouched credential; controls cover the platform-administrator and organization-scoped shapes and the holder's full `status`. The four existing suites change only in granting their default users `setup.access`; their subjects are unchanged. The five ablations are reported, not re-run here; the CI test lanes are pending (②).

10. **Docs and hold-offs — right.** The `#before-you-start` sentence and the `#reference` `status` row state what the code does; "Sign-in: not required" on the `status` row stays true. No hunk touches `install`, `installation`, `installed`, `org-packages`, the install-local doors, objectui or `packages/spec`. The mount log line's omission of `unbind` is on `main` already (`:726` there) — not this PR's.

### ② Semver level

The changeset `.changeset/24148-cloud-connection-setup-access.md` grades `'@objectstack/cloud-connection': patch`, under `fix(cloud-connection)!:`, a BREAKING banner, the `no (narrowing)` declaration, and one ADR-0087 marker, `not-required (no-migration-prescription)`.

- The PR's `Clause-②: no (narrowing)` line — **right**. The act is an accept-set narrowing at three doors and a served-set narrowing at one; nothing refused becomes accepted (①.8 on the type face). The PR body carries the same line, line-initial.
- The ADR-0087 disposition — **right**. A runtime authorization narrowing; no spec key, export, config field or stored shape moves. The `Check Changeset` job's `check-adr-0087-registration` step passed on this head ("1 declared-breaking changeset(s), each carrying an ADR-0087 disposition … [BREAKING+bang+clause-②-narrowing] not-required (no-migration-prescription)").
- The level — **wrong**. A `(narrowing)` declaration is BREAKING (AGENTS.md, Post-Task Checklist 3), and during the launch window a breaking change ships at least `minor` (`scripts/check-changeset-no-major.mjs`, "The DIRECTION ARM" and `judgeLevel`). The `Check Changeset` check-run on this head concluded `failure` on exactly this: its level axis returned `enforce` — "Moved and graded `patch`: @objectstack/cloud-connection: patch (.changeset/24148-cloud-connection-setup-access.md). None of them is graded `minor` or above. · declaration line: `Clause-②: no (narrowing)` · direction arm: `narrowing` — a BREAKING change; during the launch window it ships `minor`" — exit 1. The changeset's own sentence "shipped as `patch`: no public surface widens" states the wrong rule: the grade a breaking change owes is not conditioned on widening. The dev's local reading ("no `major` bump, exit 0") was the major guard alone — with no `pull_request` payload the level axis stands down (`no-pull-request`), so this could not be measured locally. The cited precedent (PR #24161's rest changeset) is not on `main` at the merge base and is not an input to this record; every `Clause-②: no (narrowing)` changeset on `main` grades a moved package `minor` or higher, this package's own precedent included (`.changeset/pre/23190-auth-gate-cli-sites.md`, `'@objectstack/cloud-connection': minor`).
- Remedy, one word plus one sentence: `'@objectstack/cloud-connection': minor`, and the banner reworded to the convention's sentence ("shipped as `minor` under the launch-window convention for breaking changes"). Nothing else in the changeset moves. `skip-changeset` does not apply: a released package publishes.

Gate verdicts on the head, as read in this act (39 check-runs): 25 `success`, 1 `failure` (`Check Changeset`), 8 `in_progress`, 5 `skipped`. Pending and not waited on: `Build Docs`; `Test Core` 1/6 through 6/6; `Type Check · consumer gates`. Skipped: `Console Pin Gate`, the `Dogfood Regression Gate` matrix shard, `Dogfood Verify CLI`, `Packed-tarball smoke (opt-in)`, `Temporal Conformance`. Green and material here: `Lint & Repo Gates` and every `Lint ·` lane, `Type Check · workspace` / `· source gates` / `· debt ledger`, `Build Core`, `Spec property liveness`, `Governed Surface Queue Guard` (no governed path in the file list), the single-claim and card-claims-branch checks.

### ③ Boundary flags

1. **Dev's open question — `GET /status` during a permission-store outage, signed-in caller: A (withhold, `200`, `warn`) or B (`503`).** Answered: **A, as built; no change asked.** The outage ruling's harm is an outage reported as a capability denial; `status` reports no denial — it issues no `401`/`403` — so withholding misreports nothing. It serves strictly less than it would with the store readable, never more, so no accept-set or served-set widens. The probe semantics (does the plugin answer, is the runtime bound) are the hold-off the claim named, and B would break them in exactly the window an operator is diagnosing. The three doors, where a verdict is required, re-raise and answer `503` — that is where the ruling bites, and it is honoured (①.5). The outage is logged at `warn` (`servedStatus`), so it is not silent. Both directions are pinned. Closed here, not escalated.

2. **Dev's out-of-scope note — `/install` still gates on a session alone with its `TODO: tighten`.** The hold-off held: no hunk touches `install`, `installation`, `installed` or `org-packages`. Its posture was ruled on #15353 and the carrier is the maintainer; this record escalates nothing and files nothing — it stays as the dev reported it on the card.

3. **Dev's deviations.** `test:repo` not run locally → the `Test Core` lanes are pending; a gate verdict still to come, not a finding against the diff. Consumer type-check of the `getKernel?` optional member not run locally → `Type Check · consumer gates` is pending; `· workspace` and `· source gates` are green, and ①.8 judges the member as not moving the declaration. The twice-run battery, the shallow checkout and the attribution choice are procedural; nothing to answer. One prose slip in the PR body: the datasource precedent is spelled `services/service-datasource/src/admin-routes.ts`; the file is `packages/services/service-datasource/src/admin-routes.ts`, and the code claim about it (same resolver, same field, `403 PERMISSION_DENIED`) holds there.

4. **Security review (triage `6229951531`), the four questions.** (i) Can a caller lacking `setup.access` still reach a write door's effect, or `status`'s `connection`? Not by any credential shape read here (①.1, ①.2, ①.6): anonymous `401`; key-only `401`; held `403`; signed-in-without `403`; key-beside refused; `status` narrowed for every one of these. Grants resolve through the one resolver from the kernel the session came from, and no engine fails closed (①.3, ①.4). (ii) Does the outage path fail closed on the doors? Yes — re-raised, rendered `503 SERVICE_UNAVAILABLE` by the host (①.5). (iii) Does the check run before any control-plane call or credential touch? On the three doors, yes, before all of them (①.1); on `status` the runtime's own status fetch precedes the read, as on `main`, with the runtime's credential and never the caller's, and the check decides only what is served (①.6). (iv) Is the shared permission read reused rather than re-spelled? Yes (①.3). **The boundary holds as built.** The FAIL below is on ② alone.
